feature.summary: A Managed Cloud project can store a default model. On Web a new chat in that project starts on it once; Mobile shows and applies it for Cloud chats; VS Code shows it and offers a button that opens the picker, but does not switch by itself. The CLI and Chrome have no project default.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores one model id on the project and uses it as the starting model of new chats in that project. [inferred from ProjectDefaultModelField.tsx and WebChatPage.tsx:2125-2140]
purpose.why_it_exists: Teams and individuals keep a project on the model that suits its work without choosing each time (brief S79.03).
purpose.who_uses_it: People with Managed Cloud projects on Web, Desktop, Mobile and VS Code.
problems_solved: Forgetting to change model for a project's chats.
Starting a project chat on whatever model was last used.
use_cases: A coding project defaults to a strong code model.
A notes project defaults to an economy choice.
A project keeps the Auto model as its default.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: project settings dialog, field 'Default model' (apps/web/features/projects/components/ProjectDefaultModelField.tsx:46-50; used at ProjectSettingsDialog.tsx:336).

Mobile: project overview line 'Default model: <name>' (apps/mobile/src/features/projects/components/CloudProjectOverview.tsx:70-71); applies in new Cloud chats (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx:339-348).

VS Code: project list shows the model; 'Project default model' quick pick offers 'Use <your model>' or 'No default model'; applying a project shows 'Its default model is <name>.' with a 'Choose the model' button (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/projects/projectActions.ts:320-342, 405-416).
prerequisites: A Managed Cloud project; Local and own-key projects are device-owned and not stored in the table (apps/web/db/neon/0053_projects_managed_cloud_contract.sql:1-3).
Signed in; the model must be allowed by the plan (Web field filters options).
screens_and_controls: Web: select with first option 'No default, use the model you last picked'; help text 'New chats in this project start on this model. You can still switch in any chat.' A saved value that is no longer allowed appears as '<name> (not available on your plan)' (ProjectDefaultModelField.tsx:55-78).
journey: Open project settings and choose a default model, then save.
Start a new chat inside the project.
The picker shows the project's model.
Send; you can still change the model in that chat.
feedback_and_outputs: The picker shows the project's model on a new chat.
VS Code notification text and button.
settings: Project field defaultModelId; set through the projects API.

working: Web field lists only models the plan allows and drops coming-soon models; Auto rows appear only for non-free tiers that allow them (ProjectDefaultModelField.tsx:21-38).
Save writes default_model_id through PUT /api/projects/[id] (apps/web/app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts:212) and creation reads it back (apps/web/app/api/projects/route.ts:99).
On Web, a new chat with no displayed conversation applies the project default once per project and model, only if the model is selectable (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:2123-2140).

Mobile reads defaultModelId into project details (apps/mobile/stores/projects/cloudProjectStore.ts:140-152) and shows it as the conversation model when in Cloud mode, no model shown yet, and the account may use it (chat.tsx:339-348).
VS Code stores and shows the default and offers the picker (projectActions.ts:157, 320-342, 405-416).
incomplete: VS Code does not switch the model; it opens the picker on a button press (projectActions.ts:405-416).
VS Code can only set the project default to the person's own configured model, and refuses a Local one (projectActions.ts:320-342).
Mobile reads and applies the default but no control to set it was found.
not_available: Own-key and Local projects: not stored in the cloud table.

established.statement: A project can set a default model that new chats in the project use.
Project default privacy mode was cut because it was never read; Cloud projects keep their managed label.

acceptance_criteria: Setting a default in a Web project and starting a new chat in it selects that model.
The field does not list models the plan cannot use, and shows a stale value with '(not available on your plan)'.
Choosing 'No default' stores null and new chats use the last model picked.
The default applies once per project and does not override a model the person changes mid-chat.
On Mobile a Cloud new chat in the project shows the project model if the account may use it.
VS Code shows the default model name when a project is applied and offers the picker.
inferred: A downgrade that makes the saved default unavailable should fall back without an error. The Web code simply skips an unselectable model. [inferred from WebChatPage.tsx:2136]
proposed: [proposed] Let VS Code switch directly when the default is allowed.
[proposed] Add a Mobile control to set the default.

steps.what_happens: Person saves a default in project settings; client calls PUT /api/projects/[id] with defaultModelId.
Server stores the id in user_projects.default_model_id.
On opening a new chat in the project the Web page reads the id from the project store and selects it if selectable.
The first message sends the selected model through the normal chat route (see F079-04).
Mobile and VS Code read the same project data and apply or offer it locally.

corrections.claim: Web field lists only models the plan allows and drops coming-soon models; Auto rows appear only for non-free tiers (ProjectDefaultModelField.tsx:21-38)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The plan filter applies only when billing policy is ready; when tier is null every non-coming-soon model is listed. managed_cloud rows need a non-free tier and membership in getAllowedAutoModesForTier.
corrections.correction: The field lists every non-coming-soon model until billing policy is ready; after that it lists only plan-allowed models, with Auto rows only for non-free tiers that allow them.

corrections.claim: Save writes default_model_id through PUT /api/projects/[id] (route.ts:212) and creation reads it back (projects/route.ts:99)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: PUT line 212 is correct and writes the value as given. route.ts:99 is a SELECT in the list query, not creation. Creation writes it as an INSERT column at lines 198-200.
corrections.correction: POST /api/projects inserts default_model_id (route.ts:198-200); the list query selects it (route.ts:99).

corrections.claim: Signed in; the model must be allowed by the plan (Web field filters options)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: Plan filtering is client-side only and skipped while billing is not ready. The PUT route adds the value with no plan check.
corrections.correction: The plan limit is a Web UI filter, not enforced on the server; an API client can store any id.

corrections.claim: Saved default no longer allowed: field shows '<name> (not available on your plan)'; Web apply skips an unselectable model (ProjectDefaultModelField.tsx:68-70; WebChatPage.tsx:2136)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: Label is correct, but at lines 60-63, not 68-70. The apply effect checks isSelectableModelId, not plan entitlement, so a plan-disallowed but selectable model is still applied.
corrections.correction: Web apply skips only models that are not selectable in the model store; it does not check the plan tier, unlike Mobile, which checks isSelectableModelIdForAccess.

missing_facts: Mobile applies the default with an entitlement check (isSelectableModelIdForAccess with cloudUnlocked and subscriptionTier) and requires cloud execution mode, while Web checks only selectability: apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx:339-348 vs apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:2136.
Web field lists all non-coming-soon models while billing policy is not ready (tier null): apps/web/features/projects/components/ProjectDefaultModelField.tsx:27.

Desktop has no own implementation: grep found no defaultModelId in apps/desktop/src, apps/cli or apps/extension, so Desktop depends wholly on the hosted web UI. The page marks it 'built' without saying so in section 3.
